Hi Dylan,

Thanks for the demo last week. Procurement and our security/compliance team reviewed Redwood's private deployment options and we have a couple of requirements to close procurement:

- Our external auditor needs the ability to obtain an immutable snapshot of the runtime environment (VM/container filesystem + relevant logs) for a quarterly compliance review.
- Snapshot must be delivered with a cryptographic attestation (hash + KMS-signed assertion) and ideally a hash we can store in our records.

Can you let me know what contract language you typically accept for this sort of request? We expect the MSA/Order Form to include: permitted snapshot frequency, custody/handling terms, and an auditor access process. I attached our internal audit requirements for reference.

Hi Anita — thanks for the clear note and the attachment.

We can support a few approaches; I'll loop in Legal and our Infrastructure lead to confirm feasibility and suggest contract language. High-level options we typically offer:

1) Attested snapshot: we create a time-bound snapshot of the runtime, deliver the artifact to a customer S3 (encrypted), and provide a KMS-signed hash and delivery manifest. No secrets included.
2) Auditor bastion: we provide time-limited, read-only access via a jumpbox with strict logging and session recording to satisfy auditor access needs.
3) Hybrid: snapshot + short auditor session to validate snapshot contents.

I'll get Legal and Eng to propose redlines for the MSA and Order Form that avoid open-ended escrow language but cover custody, attestation, and audit windows. Can you confirm: preferred auditor (name/email) and whether MediCore requires on-prem physical inspection or if remote evidence is acceptable?

Dylan / team,

Thanks for the heads-up. Engineering and Legal aligned on a pragmatic approach that balances MediCore's needs and our risk posture. Summary below — please share with Anita and confirm next steps.

Summary of recommended approach (short):
- Terminology: refer to the deliverable as a "custodial snapshot and attestation" (explicitly not 'escrow') in the MSA; define scope in the Order Form.
- Deliverable: Redwood will produce a read-only snapshot artifact (filesystem + specified logs) and transmit it to a customer-controlled secure bucket. The artifact will be accompanied by a KMS-signed manifest containing SHA-256 hashes of included files.
- Auditor access: Redwood will provide a short, time-limited read-only session (max 3 business days) via a monitored bastion for an approved, named auditor. Session recordings and audit logs are provided as evidence.
- Frequency & retention: Quarterly snapshots are permitted by default; each snapshot request requires a minimum 10-business-day notice. Redwood will retain delivery manifests for 12 months for auditability.
- Security protections: Snapshots exclude secret stores, private keys, and customer PII beyond what is necessary for the auditor to validate processing flows. We will redact or mask fields per the snapshot procedure.
- Liability & limitations: Limit Redwood's liability for snapshot content accuracy and state that snapshots are for compliance verification only; no ability for auditor to modify environment.

Attached are: (1) proposed MSA redlines with a new Section X (Custodial Snapshots & Auditor Access) and (2) the technical snapshot procedure describing encryption, hashing, and delivery steps.

Open items for customer confirmation:
- Preferred auditor name and contact (to approve bastion access)
- Whether remote evidence is acceptable vs. on-site inspection
- Agreement to the 10-business-day request window and 3-day access window

If Anita can confirm these items, we can prepare an Order Form addendum and send for signature (DocuSign link below). I'll mark the redlines as non-negotiable items we need Legal approval for.
